data.question: Can an operator grant be stored and consumed with the existing approval engine and no new event kind?

evidence.note: ddflow brief --item read; r-everything-managed/r-reuse-core: reused approval engine, no new event kind, knobs in [grants]
services/grants.py, api/grants.py, grant CLI, review hooks; tests/test_operator_grants.py 26 pass; pinned outputs regenerated

chunk_findings.detail: `GNT.pick(...)` is called and `a["grant"] = grant.id` is set whenever `spent` is true, before `_budget` decides whether a grant is actually needed. `_budget` has an existing past-cap allowance path that prints `[review].max_rounds = {cap}: prefer review triage` and returns `("", "")` before the new `if grant is not None` branch. In that path the round proceeds without using the grant, but the grant id is still set, and later `_cite_grant` at the outcome records `budget_grant`, consuming an operator grant for a round that never ran on it. Concretely: `max_rounds=1`, an item/gate state that hits the `prefer review triage` allowance, and an available operator grant with `--count 1`; the past-cap review consumes that grant even though `_budget` permits the round independently.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:1223

chunk_findings.detail: The function’s own docstring says it raises `GrantRefused` for an unknown item or gate, but the implementation only checks `if item not in st.items`; it never verifies that `gate` exists for that item. For an existing item `foo` with no gate `bar`, `add(..., item="foo", gate="bar", kind="review_round", count=1, reason="test")` succeeds and records a grant for a nonexistent gate instead of refusing. Later calls to `grants()`/`_used` may then call `Item.runs_of("bar")` on a gate that does not exist.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/grants.py:add

chunk_findings.detail: `pick` does not honor its documented contract: “The oldest usable one is taken first.” If the state has an older plain grant (`G1`, `when=""`) and a newer standing grant (`G2`, `when="tree_changed_after_triage"`) and the standing predicate holds, `pick(..., force=True, ctx=ctx)` returns `G2`, because it loops over all standing grants before considering any plain grant. The older usable plain grant is left unused while the newer standing grant is consumed, producing wrong `used` counts and a misleading grant report.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/grants.py:pick

chunk_findings.detail: `grants` sorts by `(g.at, g.id)` using lexicographic ID order. If two grants share the same `at` value (for example, multiple grants added within the same second), then `G10` sorts before `G2`, so the newer grant is considered older and `pick` can consume it first. This violates the module’s “oldest first” ordering after 10 grants.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/grants.py:grants

chunk_findings.detail: These tests call `_add(proj, "--when", "tree_changed_after_triage", ...)` and ignore its return code/output without asserting success. If `grant add --when` is rejected (for example because standing grants are misregistered or the count/limit check breaks), the subsequent `_state()` contains no grant, `GR.pick(...)` returns `None`, and the tests still pass. That gives a false pass and hides a regression in the standing-grant path the tests are meant to cover.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_operator_grants.py:test_a_standing_grant_does_not_apply_when_the_predicate_fails and test_a_standing_grant_is_capped_by_its_count

chunk_findings.detail: When an operator grant is present, `_budget` returns `f"operator grant {grant.id}: {grant.reason}"` and bypasses the `if force and reason.strip():` branch. So if `[review].max_rounds=1`, one round is already used, and an operator grant exists for the gate, `ddflow review --force --reason "flaky test"` picks the grant and records the operator grant reason as `forced`; the agent-supplied `--reason` text is dropped. That violates [D-review-force-with-reason], which requires the `--force --reason` text to be recorded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_budget

chunk_findings.detail: The previous #2 is not fully fixed: the new gate check only fires when `gates is not None`. A direct call `add(log, cfg, item="foo", gate="bar", kind="review_round", count=1, reason="test")` with `foo` existing but no gate `bar` still succeeds because `gates` defaults to `None`, and the function never checks `st.items["foo"]` for `bar`. The triage probe exercised the CLI path, which passes `gates`; it does not answer this default-argument path, so the function can still record an invalid grant.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/grants.py:add

chunk_findings.detail: `grants()` calls `_used` for every grant, and `_used` executes `it.runs_of(gate)` with no gate-existence guard. A grant that was valid when recorded can later refer to a gate removed from the item’s current config; then `st.items[item]` exists but lacks that gate, so `it.runs_of("missing")` raises instead of treating the stale grant as `used=0` or skipping it. Since `grants()` backs `ddflow grant list`, `ddflow review`, and `pick`, one stale grant makes all of those commands crash.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/grants.py:_used

chunk_findings.detail: Both `_add(proj)` calls ignore their return code. If the second standing `_add` (`--when tree_changed_after_triage`) is rejected, the state still contains only the plain G1, and the final `GR.pick(... force=True, ctx=held).id == "G1"` assertion still passes. The test is meant to verify oldest plain beats newer standing when both exist, but it passes in that failure mode and hides a regression in standing-grant add/pick ordering.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_operator_grants.py:test_the_oldest_usable_grant_is_taken_first_standing_or_not

chunk_findings.detail: The test ignores `RV._scope`’s return value and checks only the pre-populated local `a["grant"] == ""`. If `_scope` no longer lets the past-cap `on_exceed="warn"` round proceed grant-free and instead refuses the review, it still does not set `a["grant"]`, so the assertion passes. The test would not catch a regression that disables the on_exceed=warn grant-free allowance, which its docstring says this test pins.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_operator_grants.py:test_a_round_the_budget_allows_anyway_does_not_spend_a_grant

chunk_findings.detail: The existing guard `if item.startswith("item/") and gate == "review" and not (force and reason.strip()):` runs before the newly added `if grant is not None:` branch. In the exact case the new code describes — a `review_round` grant that stands in for the free-text reason, or a standing grant that “needs no `--force` at all” — this guard is true (no agent `reason` when the grant supplies it, or no `force` for a standing grant), so `_budget` returns `("", "")` before ever checking `grant`. The result is that `a["grant"]` is later set to `""` because `forced` is empty, so the selected operator grant is never cited in `round_evidence`, meaning it is neither consumed nor reported in the per-session “grants used” report, breaking grant accounting for the common `item/...` / `review` gate case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_budget

chunk_findings.detail: The test blesses a path where `[review].on_exceed = "warn"` lets a review past `max_rounds` proceed with `force=True` and an empty `reason`, and asserts no grant is consumed. That conflicts with [D-review-force-with-reason], which requires `ddflow review --force --reason` so the extra round is recorded and the gate is listed under `gate list --refuted` rather than being silently allowed. Concretely: set `on_exceed=warn`, have one completed round at `max_rounds=1`, then invoke `RV._scope(... force=True, reason="")`; the documented behavior is that the review runs with no reason and no grant, so the reason/grant audit trail required by the decision is bypassed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_operator_grants.py: test_a_round_the_budget_allows_anyway_does_not_spend_a_grant

chunk_findings.detail: The fix for the prior D-review-force-with-reason finding does not answer the original input. In `_budget`, the `if done == cap:` branch is still executed before the new `if grant is not None:` and the `if force and reason.strip():` branches. With `[review].max_rounds = 1` and one round already used (`_rounds_used` returns 1), `done == cap` is true, so `_budget` returns `("", "")`; the operator grant branch is never reached, `forced` is empty, and `a["grant"]` is set to `""`. Therefore the agent-supplied `--reason "flaky test"` is still dropped rather than recorded. The probe `test_the_agents_reason_is_kept_beside_the_grant` only passes because it must reach the `done > cap` grant branch, not the reported `done == cap` scenario, so [D-review-force-with-reason] is still violated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_budget

chunk_findings.detail:
The `add` function signature places a required keyword-only argument after optional keyword-only arguments:

`... when: str = "", requested_agent: str = "", gates: Collection[str],`

Python rejects a non-default argument following a default argument, including in keyword-only position, with `SyntaxError: non-default argument follows default argument`. Because this is a module-level function definition, importing `ddflow.services.grants` fails immediately, so every command that imports it (`ddflow grant add`, `ddflow grant list`, and review/gate paths using this module) crashes before doing anything.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/grants.py:add

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test for the prior gate-check bug only asserts `inspect.signature(GR.add).parameters["gates"].default is inspect.Parameter.empty`. It never calls `GR.add(..., gates=None)` with an invalid gate, so it does not exercise the gate validation. Because a required parameter can still accept an explicit `None`, an implementation can still contain the original `if gates is not None:` guard; for example, `GR.add(EventLog(proj, "probe"), _cfg(), item="T1", gate="no_such_gate", kind="review_round", count=1, reason="r", gates=None)` would still skip the gate check and record an invalid grant, while this test would pass.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_operator_grants.py:test_add_cannot_skip_the_gate_check

chunk_findings.detail: `untriaged=sum(1 for r in rows if r["trie"] == "untriaged")` indexes the row key `"trie"`, but review rows use the triage status key `"triage"`. Given a normal review item with a non-empty `_FR._rows(it, gate)` list, this comprehension raises `KeyError: 'trie'` on the first row, so every standing-grant predicate requiring `GNT.Ctx` crashes instead of evaluating the grant.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_grant_ctx

chunk_findings.detail: The new `if grant is not None:` branch is placed after the pre-existing early return that blocks an extra review round when there is no `--force --reason` (the branch that says `[review].max_rounds = {cap}: prefer review triage.` and returns `("", "")`). Because that early return runs before the grant branch, a standing `review_round` grant that the change itself says “needs no `--force` at all” is never reached: with `max_rounds=1`, `on_exceed=block`, one completed round, and a valid operator grant supplied, `_budget` returns `("", "")` and blocks the review before ever inspecting the grant. The previous triage did not address this: the probe `grep 'startswith("item/")'` found nothing only because the guard does not contain that substring; the offending condition is the missing `--force`/`--reason` guard that still precedes the new branch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:1426 (_budget)

chunk_findings.detail: `add` only checks `gate not in gates` and `item not in st.items`; it never verifies that the named gate actually belongs to the named item. In the CLI path `gates` is the set of all configured gate names, so `ddflow grant add --item docs --gate review --kind review_round --count 1 --reason "extra"` succeeds even when `docs` has no `review` gate. The recorded grant can never be picked (`pick` requires `(g.item, g.gate, g.kind) == (item, gate, kind)`), so the operator is told the grant was accepted but it is unusable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/grants.py add

chunk_findings.detail: The test blesses `RV._budget(cfg, "T1", "critic", 1, True, "", ..., grant=g)` returning `why == ""` with only the grant id cited, i.e. once a grant exists, `ddflow review --force` without `--reason` past `[review].max_rounds` is accepted. This violates [D-review-force-with-reason], which requires the forced round to carry a reason and be represented under `gate list --refuted`; the operator's reason at grant-add time is not the reviewing agent's `--reason`. The earlier probe that the pre-existing `_budget` guard was absent does not answer this: it only made the no-reason-with-grant path reachable, and this test codifies it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_operator_grants.py:test_force_past_the_cap_with_a_grant_needs_no_free_text_and_cites_the_id

chunk_findings.detail: The branch `if not force or not reason.strip(): ... return "", ""` executes before `if grant is not None:` is ever checked. With `[review].max_rounds = 1`, one round already used, and a valid standing grant, a review called without `--force`/`--reason` hits that refusal branch first. The returned `forced` is empty, so the caller sets `a["grant"] = ""`; the grant is never cited or consumed. This contradicts the function’s own docstring that “a standing one needs no `--force` at all,” and it breaks the standing-grant path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_budget

chunk_findings.detail: The `--count` help text says the cap is `[review].grant_max_count`, but the new knobs added by this change are `grants.max_count` and `grants.ttl_h` (see `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.grants.max_count.toml`). An operator who follows the documented knob sets `[review] grant_max_count`, which does not control grants, so the advertised configuration does not work.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/grants.py:21

chunk_findings.detail: The second assertion passes item "T2" even though the `proj` fixture only adds "T1", so `st.items` has no "T2". This does not exercise the “grant does not cross items” property for an existing item: an implementation that treats an unknown item as having no matching grant can still pass while incorrectly matching a T1 grant for an existing T2 with the same gate. Add a second task "T2" with the critic gate and assert a T1 grant is not picked for that existing T2 to actually cover the claimed behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_operator_grants.py:test_a_grant_does_not_cross_gates_or_items
